reason: The hypothesis makes specific, non-trivial claims about composition–property relationships and deformation mechanisms in HfNbTaTiZr, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the precise thresholds or nonmonotonic trends proposed.
premises: Nb/Ta reduction to 10% increases strength and modulus via solid-solution strengthening
Nb/Ta increase to 30% reduces strength and modulus due to excessive lattice mismatch
Ti/Zr substitution initially lowers mechanical performance by increasing lattice strain and defects
Ti/Zr substitution at higher levels partially recovers strength via atomic reordering
Elevated temperature (300–1200 K) degrades strength, stiffness, and solid-solution integrity
